steps: Identify the shape (or split compound shapes)
Substitute the measurements (watch units and use perpendicular height)
Calculate and include correct units (cm², m², etc.)
method_card.title: Area & Perimeter
method_card.content:
Rectangle: Area = \(l \times w\), Perimeter = \(2(l + w)\). Triangle: Area = \(\frac{1}{2} \times b \times h\). Parallelogram: Area = \(b \times h\) (perpendicular height, not slant).

Trapezium: Area = \(\frac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h\). Circle: Area = \(\pi r^2\), Circumference = \(2\pi r\) or \(\pi d\). For compound shapes, split into simpler shapes, find each area, then add or subtract.
method_card.example:
Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm.

Area = \(\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20\) cm²

problem_bank.bronze_description: Find the area or perimeter of one standard shape by putting numbers straight into its formula.
problem_bank.silver_description: Halves and circles, compound shapes, and working a formula backwards to find a missing length.
problem_bank.gold_description: Sectors and arcs (a fraction of a circle), composite perimeters, and rings between two circles.

bronze.title: Bronze: one shape, one formula
steps: Name the shape, then pick its formula. Rectangle: length × width. Triangle: ½ × base × height. Parallelogram: base × height. Trapezium: ½(a + b) × height.
Put the measurements in and work it out. Halve for a triangle; do not halve for a parallelogram.
Perimeter is the distance round the edge; area is the space inside. Give area in square units, like cm².

example.question: Find the area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 6 cm.

steps.label: Check the halving
steps.content: 8 × 6 = 48, and a triangle is half of its rectangle

silver.title: Silver: halves, circles and missing sides
steps: Semicircle: find the full circle, then halve. A semicircle's perimeter is π r + 2 r (curve plus diameter).
Compound shape: work out each piece, then add or subtract. A cut-out is subtracted.
Missing length: put what you know into the formula and solve backwards, for example height = area ÷ (½ × base).

example.question: A semicircle has diameter 10 cm. Find its area to 1 decimal place.

gold.title: Gold: sectors, arcs and rings
steps: A sector is a fraction of a circle: fraction = angle ÷ 360. Sector area = (angle ÷ 360) × π r².
Arc length is the same fraction of the circumference: (angle ÷ 360) × 2 π r.
Annulus (ring): subtract the two areas, π R² − π r², never the radii.
